# FDG5060

> DO take one parameter to the protected method that raises an event.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.4 Event Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5060
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: The method '{0}' that raises an event should take one parameter

FDG5060 reports an externally visible protected (or protected internal) method named "On" followed by the name of an event of its class or a base class, when it does not take exactly one parameter. Overrides are not reported; their parameters come from the base method. A raising method with another name is not seen. The name e and the event argument type, which the body adds, are not checked. Changing the parameters of a protected method changes the public API, so the fix is breaking.

## From the book

The parameter should be named `e` and should be typed as the event argument class.

```csharp
protected virtual void OnAlarmRaised(AlarmRaisedEventArgs e){
  AlarmRaised?.Invoke(this, e);
}
```
